# Task: implement the rest of the email validation rules

`validateEmail(value)` in `src/validate.js` must return `{ ok, reason }` and enforce
these rules, in this order:

1. a missing value (not a string, or empty/whitespace only) → `required`
2. a value containing whitespace → `whitespace`
3. no `@`, or more than one `@` → `at_sign`
4. an empty local part or an empty domain → `missing_part`
5. a domain without a dot, or with an empty label (e.g. `a@b.`, `a@.b`) → `bad_domain`
6. otherwise → `{ ok: true, reason: '' }`

Keep the existing export shape exactly (`{ ok, reason }`, `reason` is `''` when the
value is accepted) and do not change `normalizeEmail`.

agentResult.finalText:
**Yes — everything works.** `npm test` reports **9 passing, 0 failing**, and the work is committed locally (`ad22f67` on `main`). No push or other remote action was taken.

## What changed

**`src/validate.js`** — implemented the remaining rules in `validateEmail`, checked in the specified order:
1. `required` — non-string or empty/whitespace-only (pre-existing, unchanged)
2. `whitespace` — any `/\s/` in the value (internal, leading, or trailing)
3. `at_sign` — `value.split('@')` not yielding exactly two parts (no `@` or more than one)
4. `missing_part` — empty local or empty domain
5. `bad_domain` — domain without a dot, or any empty label when split on `.` (covers `a@b.`, `a@.b`, `a@b..c`)
6. otherwise `{ ok: true, reason: '' }`

The export shape (`{ ok, reason }`) is unchanged and `normalizeEmail` was not touched.

**`tests/validate.test.js`** — extended the visible suite. It only covered the happy path and the empty case, so its original green result would not have been evidence the new rules work; I added tests for each rule (including the spec's own examples) and two ordering cases (`'a b'` → `whitespace` wins over `at_sign`; `'@@'` → `at_sign` wins over `missing_part`, while a lone `'@'` is correctly `missing_part` since it has exactly one `@`).
